utterances.text: Now I will return to the announcement on the radio about weapons. You stated that the announcement said the Muslim population of the villages, et cetera, had to hand over their weapons. When was this announcement approximately? Which month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: At the end of May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Were there some weapons in your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: To your knowledge were these weapons handed over or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: At any point in May was your village or -- I am now referring to Hrustovo as such. Was in May Hrustovo shelled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: When was it? Was it before the announcement to hand over weapons or after?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: To a slight degree, before the announcement. And then afterwards it was continued.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Indirectly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What do you mean indirectly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: My father owned one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And what happened to this weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: I handed it in to my neighbours, who later handed it over to the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And is it correct to say that after you handed over this weapon you left this hamlet and you went to another hamlet within the village of Kljevci?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: When was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: At the end of May 1992. I can't say the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: How long did you stay in that other settlement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: A month.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: How many people were there in that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Together with the women, there were about 50 inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I will like to refer you to your statement when you said that at one point you went to a very small hamlet with only three houses and then you moved from this -- from that place. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So what made you to move from that small hamlet with only three houses to another place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Well, one day a Serb came who was a neighbour to that small hamlet that I had come to. He was angry. He was nervous. He told us that the inhabitants of Begici, a small hamlet that also belongs to Kljevci, that they had all been killed. Of course men, I'm talking about men. And he was afraid that the same could happen to us. And so he invited us to come over to his home, his house, and we agreed and we headed off to his place.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And were you able to stay in his place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Briefly. Not for long.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Why weren't you able to stay there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Because when he brought us there, he went off somewhere. And when he returned, he said that because of his own security, he mustn't continue keeping us in his house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Then he told us that we would go to Kenjari, a hamlet inhabited by Muslims, and that they would provide guards to protect us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: In -- so now we are in the place where you referred before that there were approximately 50 people; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes, including us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the hamlet of Kenjari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: About three weeks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And what happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Around the 27th or the 28th - I am not sure of the date - at dawn we were woken up by our mothers or members of our family who said that the Serbs had entered the village, that they were starting to search the houses, and that they had said that we should all go to the crossroads that was just in front of the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you see these Serbs who went to your village and started searching houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Who were they? Were they soldiers or civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: They were armed inhabitants of the village of Kljevci. They were Serbs. They were armed and in uniform, and they were searching the houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: When you say they were in uniforms, what kind of uniforms did they wear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: SMB, olive-grey. Some of them in camouflage uniforms or coloured ones. I don't know how you call them. Some in jeans. Others had a shirt or a pullover of the same SMB colour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you see any insignia on uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes. They were mostly the insignia of the Serb army.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you know who were -- who was in command of these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Their commander was there too. He was a Serb, an inhabitant of Kljevci, and his name was Milorad Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you know this person from before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So how did you learn his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: While we were staying in the hamlet of Kenjari, he would come to that village several times and he spoke to people in that village, so that I learnt his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: This Milorad Mijatovic, was he in a military uniform or in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: He always wore a uniform, and he was some sort of an officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: When you say "some sort of an officer," can you be again more specific?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Maybe a sergeant or something like that. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You said that these people searched your houses. Did they found -- did they find anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Not what they were looking for.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And what they were looking for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: They were allegedly looking for weapons, which we didn't have in our possession.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You also stated that you were ordered together at the crossroads. Did you do it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And what happened at that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: When they finished with the search of the houses, they came back and they said that all people of age, up to the oldest men, must go for interrogation to their command, whereas the women and children could return to the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And were you taken for the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did all the people who entered the village and did the searches accompanied you for that interrogation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Not all of them. Some of them took us for interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you know names of people who accompanied you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Some of their names, yes. Zeljko Karanovic. Then there was Nikola Balac. There was a young man called Misko Erak. Then there were two Damjanovic brothers. I don't know their first name.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: This Zeljko Karanovic, did he wear any kind of uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes. He wore the uniform of reservists of the Serb army.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Were -- how many people were gathered for this interrogation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Twenty.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So you left Kenjari, and where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: First they told us this we were going to the school where allegedly their command was; however, we didn't enter the school, we didn't even look inside. We went on beyond the school. We reached the house owned by a Croat whose name was Marko Juric.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And when you reached the house, what happened there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: When we got there, Zeljko was like the leader of the group and he told us to wait in the yard there, that he was allegedly going for the command who would come to interrogate us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did he return the same day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So when did he return?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: He returned the next day late in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: The following day when Karanovic returned, did anybody else came to see you to Marko Juric's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: A man came -- actually, three of them. One of them introduced himself and said his name was Vlado Vrkes, and he said that he was the president of the SDS in Sanski Most. He asked us what we were doing there. The older men answered that we had been brought there for interrogation. He said that we had nothing to fear and he told us that we would most probably be exchanged for Serbs in Eastern Bosnia and that nothing would happen to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And after this, the person who introduced himself as Vlado Vrkes left; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes. He stayed there very briefly and he left.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You also said that Zeljko Karanovic returned the following day, the day when Vlado Vrkes came to see you. After Zeljko Karanovic returned, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: When he arrived, he said that we should get ready, that we were going to Blazevici for interrogation, where allegedly their command was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to ask you if you would be able to point at the map where the hamlet of Blazevici was or is?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It is also again not marked on this map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Somewhere around here roughly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you write a "B" there, please, where you think that this hamlet is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And now, sir, next to that "B," put your initials, please, and also put them where you had put the letter "H" at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just initials again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Okay. Now we can remove the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This will go under seal, sir. You don't have to worry because it will --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: But it was on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Pardon?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's not broadcasted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: When you reached this -- before you reached Blazevici hamlet, did you -- did anybody else join your group of people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes. Just after we had passed through the hamlet of Zukici, where the Zukici family lived, the route took us through a small wood, and when we emerged another two Serb soldiers came out of the woods.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: When you said "soldiers," did they wear uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you see any insignia on them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes. The three -- the Serbian three-coloured flag on their caps.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you still remember their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Mico Djukic and his brother Milutin.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you know these people before, or how did you learn their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: I didn't know them before. When they joined us, we noticed they were going behind us. And then I asked my friends when we were staying at Kenjari and they told me that their names were Djukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So after these two persons joined your group, you reached the hamlet of Blazevici. What happened there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: First we were taken in front of a house, and then when we arrived we saw that nothing had remained of that house. And then we headed for another house. It was half a stable, half a house, actually. And Zeljko broke into the house by kicking the door, and he looked into it briefly and said that we could go in and that he would go fetch the command for it to interrogate us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you all go in in the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So who went there? Who went inside of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: I went into the house and a few younger men who were with us. And the older ones were sitting in the front of the house and were arguing with them whether they would go in or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the owner of that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: I think his name was Dujo Banovic. But he moved out of that house, perhaps in the '70s.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And how did you learn this name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: When I spoke with some friends and told them what had happened, then they told me that it must have been that house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So we stopped when you said that some of you went inside of that house. What happened then after you entered that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: When I went in, some were already sitting there on a sheet in the hay. They sat on that hay. And then I approached the window. There were two very small windows. I opened one of them, and one of my relatives told me that it would be better to shut the window and not to create problems. And then I moved towards an old stove, where there was a container with something inside. Whether it was flour or sugar or salt, I do not know -- I don't know. When I moved away, these people were at the door still arguing with the Serbs outside, whether they would go in or not. And then all of a sudden they began shouting, "A bomb." And then we heard an impact on the -- on planks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: When you heard this noise, what was your reaction? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: I jumped out of the window.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And what followed after you jumped out of the window?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: We heard an explosion. And when I got up -- the window was fairly high from the ground. And when I got up, Mico Djukic ran up to the corner of the house and he fired at me and at another person.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: He started firing at you. So what did you do at that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: I bent behind a big stone that was there in front of the house, and the other friend started running away. When the firing stopped, I went with him, because under the house there was a big hole, about 20 metres in diameter. There were lots of -- there was growth all over it. There were weeds. He had fallen. I ran up to him, and then my friend emerged from the hole first. There was about clear ground from 200 metres from that hole near a woods, and my friend started running away. Then Mico ran towards us. He had an easier way to go. He didn't have to go through the weeds. And when I emerged from that hole, I was about 5 metres or 10 metres from Mico Djukic. Luckily for me he had already fired all his bullets. And when he saw me, he was to have changed his bullets, put in new bullets. I saw that I had no opportunity to run away because he would have hit me, as I was 200 metres away. And then I jumped back into the hole from which I had emerged.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You jumped in the hole. How far from the house was this hole?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: As I said, about 20 metres in diameter, the hole's width was. And the house was on the very edge of that hole. About 20 metres from the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Could you see what went on in the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Could you hear what went on in the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: The answer was yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: So, sorry. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. I heard "da". I know that that was yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So what did you hear from the hole? What was happening in the house or in front of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Mico, who was shooting at the person I mentioned, he returned to the entrance of the house, and then people were being thrown out of the house. They were told to put up their hands. And after an argument and swearing, I heard a blast of fire, and it was directed against those people.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You were still hiding in that hole when you heard the firing. How long does it -- how long did it last?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: About two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: After they stopped shooting, what else did you hear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: First I heard the Mico who saw me going back into the hole, he said there was someone else there in the valley, and then he called me, "Come out of the hole or I'll come down and slit your throat."

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So at that point did you come out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What followed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Then I heard from the opposite side of the hole where I was in that he was going down, coming down. It is the part below the house. He was climbing down. I heard his steps and the twigs breaking underneath his feet. There he found a person. He fired two bullets, and then I learnt that that person had been killed. Then he came back from that hole, and then he tried -- he asked for another bomb from his soldier friends. And luckily for me they didn't have any more bombs. And then they started shooting at that hole. Luckily I was not hit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Before you -- when you jumped out of the window, you said that there was someone who jumped together with you. Do you know who was him? What was his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Ina Muharem [As interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you say Ina Muharem?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Kenjar Muharem.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you. After they stopped shooting in the hole in which you were, what did you hear or what -- what did follow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Then they began to search those people who had been killed, looking for money or I don't know what. I don't think that they actually found money, because these were very poor people. Some of them were employed in Slovenia and they had Slovenian ID. Then they were swearing and so on. Then they began carrying them into the house. I know that they were saying that one or some of them were heavy, and they kept -- and they said one of them had 100 kilos.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: After you heard that they took them inside, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: They brought them into the house, and then the house started burning. They had set fire to the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: After you saw -- were you able from the hole, were you able to see that the house was on fire from the hole?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So after the house was set on fire or started burning, how long the soldiers or the people stayed --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yeah. There was -- there wasn't -- excuse me. My question was: Were you able to see the house on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And there was an answer yes, but it's not on there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. Again, for the record, could you -- could I ask you, Madam Richterova, to repeat your question, and to the witness to repeat his answer. I'm sorry about this, sir, but unfortunately your answer did not appear in the transcript. Madam Richterova, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Were you able to see from the hole that the house was on fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: After the house started burning, how long -- how long did the soldiers or the people who were at the place stay there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: They stayed about an hour or two, until it became dark. It was evening there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: After they left, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: I still -- I was still in the hole. I wasn't sure whether they had left or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And how long in -- how long did you stay in that hole?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Until the following day at dawn.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Then I moved 200 or 300 metres into a woods. I don't think it would have been a good idea for me to have stayed near that house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Which village did you want to reach?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: I wanted to return to my village of Hrustovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And is it correct to state that at the end you managed to get to Tomina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: On the way from Blazevici to Tomina, were you able to see houses in villages which you passed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes. I stayed in a house -- I spent the night in a stable. I was in my own house. And then I visited a few more houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What was the -- what was the condition of that houses which you saw in your hamlet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: They were burnt down.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: After you reached Tomina, were there some other refugees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes. From Hrustovo and Vrhpolje and partially from Kamicak.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What was their nationality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: They were all Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Tomina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Four days.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And what made you to move from Tomina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Why did you move from Tomina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: I left because in the morning the Serb army and police came. There was a police vehicle there and had a loudspeaker, saying that all refugees from Kamicak, Vrhpolje, and Tomina should go to the crossroads nearby and should wait there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You said the Serb army and police came. How did you know or why do you say that it was the Serb army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Simply because they were Serbs. They can't be Hungarians in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You went to the crossroad, and where were you taken then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Then we were transported by bus to the hall of the former Krings factory in Sanski Most, and about 600 people gathered there, men, women, and children.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Krings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: A month.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did women also stay with you in Krings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: The women spent one night, and then the next day they were transported to Eastern or Central Bosnia, to Gracanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you briefly tell us the condition in Krings. Where were you taken? How does it look -- how did it look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: It was an empty hall of the former company. There was a faucet there and several pallets and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Where did you sleep?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: We slept on the pallets.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you have water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes. There was a sink inside.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you have toilets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: No. We went to the toilet in the hole of a machine that was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What about food? What kind of food did you receive when in Krings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: At the beginning our mothers or relatives would bring us food. At the beginning my mother was able to enter, and later on she was not able to enter.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So the food was provided by your relatives; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Who guarded you in Krings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: At the beginning, Serb soldiers. About 15 days later, the police came.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: How were you treated in -- while you were in Krings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: While we were guarded by these soldiers, no one touched us, no one beat us, no one mistreated us. But when the police came, then it all started. They began beating and torturing us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: When you are saying "beating and torturing," what -- did they use any tools while beating you or did they use just their hands?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: With batons, with rifles, with boots, with the rod of a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: While in Krings, were you interrogated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes. One day I think the main person from the police in Sanski Most came, and he said in the next few days interrogation would take place, and then there would be a procedure according to which some people would be let go, would be released, and others not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What kind of questions were you asked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: The questions were: Where were you? What did you do? What did you do in the past months? Whom were you with? Did you have weapons? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: During the time you were in Krings, did you witness anyone -- anyone who had died?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes. A man died as a result of a beating. He was beaten up, and the next morning he died.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you see who did the beating?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: I apologise. The people who brought him, it was probably them, they beat him and the guards that were already there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You said "the people who brought him." Where was he brought from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: I'm not sure. Probably from his home.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you know the name of this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Edhem Music or Edhem Masic. I don't know. I didn't know him from earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: From whom did you learn the name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: A neighbour of -- one of his neighbours was there, and he knew him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And is it correct to state that you were released on 4th of August, and on 18th of August you joined a convoy to Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: When you were released on 4th of August, who released you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: One of the guards released me, a policeman. He brought a slip of paper, on the basis of which I was released.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: In 1996 did you participate on the on-site investigation and exhumation of remains of bodies in Sanski Most, particularly in this place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Was it -- was it in January when you were in Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I only want to show the witness on-site investigation report which already has been exhibited under P795. And I'm showing these documents to the witness just for completeness of this whole exhumation procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: This is an on-site investigation report in which it's stated that you were present with other people in Sanski Most, and among them was Judge Draganovic and others, as you can see on the -- in the document. And you took them to the Blazevici hamlet where this incident happened; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Based on this on-site investigation, is it correct to state that you also -- you also provided your statement to the Judge Draganovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Then there is a document which has been exhibited P796. I don't think that we need to show this document to the witness because he wasn't present during the medical examination. But this is the report which describes the location of the mass grave, the exhumation, and the medical examination with the conclusion that it is evident from the bones recovered in the torched house in Kenjari that they are human bones belonging to a number of persons of different ages. The forensic experts were unable to specify the exact number of the deceased in the torched house because not all bones had been recovered in the course of the excavation. And it's stated that the bones were exposed to high temperature. And then I have the last document. If we could show this document the witness. It is -- excuse me. It is P797. This document is official report dated 22nd of October, 1996. And it's a report on forensic and operative measures taken and were carried out during the exhumations and identification of bodies. And I only want to show the page with names of people who were identified in mass grave Vrhpolje 9. Can we show the witness page number 0 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sorry, Madam Richterova. Are you sure it's Vrhpolje or it's Hrustovo 9?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It states -- yeah. This is -- it's Hrustovo 9. And in the English translation -- sorry. It's my -- it's my fault. I apologise. It's Hrustovo 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't worry. Nothing is going to happen to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes. Hrustovo 9 mass grave. And if we can show the witness page 00454592.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you have a look at this list of names and confirm whether these people are -- these names are those of people who were with you in Blazevici on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: There were 18 of us -- of them with me. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I have concluded my direct examination. I don't have further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Don't -- don't rush, because I think before you start with your cross-examination we're going to have a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, no. Your Honours, I have -- I have a certain --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I have a certain objection to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Please go ahead, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Because the answer of the witness was "The first 18. The rest I don't know." And it's -- it's line 64, 5. He says Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. exactly: "The first 18, yes. And the rest I don't know."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what he answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That is right. And that's not in the transcript. So if my learned colleague can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Here we have "There were 18 of us -- of them with me. Yes," yes. So it's completely different.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes. I can ask the witness to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I ask you to have a look at names under Hrustovo 9 mass graves. There follow Hrustovo 10 single graves. And I do not expect that you know the people. Because this is a complete list. If you know the other names, please state you know the other names. But my question was specifically about the names under Hrustovo 9, mass grave.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: That is whey had in mind, Hrustovo 9. There are 18 men there. And after that, this individual grave, Hrustovo 10, I don't know about those men.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It's correct. My --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's clear, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: My question was only to Hrustovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you recognise under these 18 names people who were in -- in Blazevici with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We can stop here for the time being. We'll have a break of 15 minutes, resuming at twenty to 6.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who is going first? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are now going to be cross-examined by Mr. Ackerman, who is the lead counsel for Radoslav Brdjanin. Please understand that Mr. Ackerman is doing his duty here. And the rule is that unless I stop you from answering the question, you are expected to answer the question. Okay. Mr. Ackerman, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'd like to go into private session very briefly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'd like the witness to have an opportunity to see his statement to the OTP of 18 March 2000.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Sir, I think the part that I want to refer you to you will find -- let's see if I can help you -- you'll find it over on page 3. It's the fourth paragraph down, beginning with the word "Buduci Da Sam." Do you find the sentence I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Unfortunately not yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Page 3, fourth paragraph from the top, you'll see the word "Buduci Da Sam." Are you on a page that has a "3" at the bottom right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: No. I was looking at something else.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I think you've now found what I'm referring to, have you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: All right. What -- the English translation that I have indicates that you told the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor that the war in Hrustovo lasted only one month.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you elaborate on that at all? Can you tell us what you mean that the war in Hrustovo only lasted a month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Let me see. After the first shooting that started there in our village, the shelling started the same day. The second or third day there was the surrender of weapons. And then the Serb army entered the village. There was a small-scale resistance. As far as I know, only one man opened fire, but this I heard from others. Then the women and children and some men were driven to the Tomina village. Some of the men. The majority of the men were taken to camps of Manjaca or Betonirka or to some schools. And then after that there was a small amount of resistance. And after that -- after a month, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'd like the registrar to give me the next two numbers for Brdjanin exhibits, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next one is DB91.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. And then 92, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes. If the usher could assist me now. This stack is all DB91. Give one of them to the Prosecutor and then give the rest of them to Ms. Registrar, and then when she gets through doing what she's doing, give one of each to the witness, please. And I only have two of them marked, so ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can we have BD92.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes. It's BD92.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not BT92, but DB or BD 92. Okay. It has been corrected. We were still in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Sir, you have before you two pieces of paper, DB91, DB92. One of them is the first page from your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor. The second is the last page from your statement with Judge Draganovic. And my question is just very, very simple: Just confirm for me, if you will, that on both of those documents the signature that appears there is your signature. I should say, one of the signatures is your signature on each document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: I do confirm it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: All right. On the second document, does the name Zijad Ibric appear there anywhere, BD92, the one you're looking at. Your Honour, I'm going to withdraw that question. We can all see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Ackerman. Mr. Zecevic or Madam Fauveau, I'm sorry. As you may have gathered, sir, the cross-examination of the first of the two Defence teams is over. You are now going to be cross-examined by the Defence team -- by Madam Fauveau, who is co-counsel defending General Momir Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The documents will go under seal. I also noticed for the record that the last two minutes, three minutes there has been confusion in -- whether it's BT -- DB or BD. In some instances it's referred to as BD, and in other instances it's referred to as DB. We have to be clear --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think we're doing DB and DT.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. But they are DB's but sometimes they appear as BD.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I neglected to move the admission of those two documents, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: They will be admitted later, Mr. Ackerman. Yes, Madam Fauveau. Sorry for interrupting you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you spoke of checkpoints that existed in your area. Could you tell us when those checkpoints were established.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: I can't give you a precise answer, but I think around the middle of April or the beginning of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that reservists, policemen were on those checkpoints, and that at one checkpoint there was the military police. Could you tell us where that checkpoint manned by military policemen was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: The military police were manning -- were stationed at the crossroads of the Sanski Most-Prijedor main road and the other road leading to Palanka, or rather, Bosanska Krupa.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you pass through that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So you saw those men that you describe as military policemen; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you describe their uniforms.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: They were wearing white belts, and that is a clear sign that they were military police. But otherwise, they were wearing camouflage uniforms or whatever they call them.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see the insignia on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: No. I didn't look closely.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And could you tell us approximately on what date you passed through that checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Ten years later I really cannot remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether it was in April or in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: I think it was still in April.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned reservists at other checkpoints. When you say "reservists," do you have the Territorial Defence in mind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: I mean the reservists who were the Serb army. Simply they were people that I knew. A man, for instance, who used to be a butcher suddenly became a reservist. I don't know what you mean when you say "the Territorial Defence."

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have in front of you the statement that you gave to the Bosnian authorities in 1996?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: The last part.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Prosecutor please give the witness the statement to the Bosnian authorities dated the 12th of January, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the middle of that page, you spoke of Milorad Mijatovic, who was allegedly the commander of the Serb villagers who were organised in the Territorial Defence. I'm referring to that Territorial Defence that you mentioned on page 1 of that statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: That means the Serbian Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I'm talking about the Territorial Defence. I didn't indicate of what ethnicity they were. Do you agree that the reservists you are mentioning and who were manning the checkpoint belonged to that Territorial Defence, allegedly Serb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that there were soldiers in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that those soldiers were also civilians who had been mobilised; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Those mobilised civilians, did they also belong to the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat his answer. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that the soldiers were in Sanski Most, which period are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Madam Fauveau. We have -- because we have a slight problem here. Sir, you were asked the following question: Those mobilised civilians, did they also belong to the Territorial Defence? You gave an answer, but the interpreter wasn't -- could not hear you well, and we would like to know what your answer was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said possibly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Sorry, Madam Fauveau. You may repeat your question now, the last one, and it was "When you say that the soldiers were in Sanski Most, which period are you referring to?"

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. And thank you for intervening.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: A smaller number of soldiers were there from the very beginning of 1992, but for instance, I don't know exactly. As of March, there were larger numbers because they had withdrawn from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And during this period of March and April 1992, did you go to Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes, but not very frequently.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you personally see those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you describe their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: They were wearing SMB olive-grey of the former Yugoslav People's Army. Then some were in camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that in Sanski Most there were people wearing different uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke of the return of weapons that the Serbs announced on the radio calling on the Muslims to hand over their weapons; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you handed over a gun that belonged to your father to a neighbour; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And this neighbour, to whom you gave this weapon, he was a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know what he did with that weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Later on I heard from these other women who were in the hamlet of Handanovici that he took the rifles to Zegar. You could see that on the map. And he handed them over to the Serbs and he never came back.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You personally did not see that person leave your village to go to Zegar, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: During the shelling of Hrustovo that you referred to, you yourself were not in Hrustovo, were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: For a while I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And during this first period, was there any damage in Hrustovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that when you left your village you left to go to a small hamlet and a Serb came, somebody called Djurica Mijatovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did this Mijatovic also belong to the Serb army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: To the army or to the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: I am unable to say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: This Djurica Mijatovic, was he dressed in a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: He had a shirt, an SMB shirt as part of a uniform, and the bottom were jeans.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So he wasn't wearing the kind of uniform that regular soldiers wore; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you mention the Serb army, you mean any Serb who was wearing any part of a uniform and carrying a weapon; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And this Djurica Mijatovic, he told you to leave that hamlet and you went to Kenjari from there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: No. We went to his house.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And from his house to Kenjari; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Weren't you escorted by Serbs from Djurica Mijatovic's house towards Kenjari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: We were.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And who were those Serbs who were accompanying you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: They were local Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: They were also members of the Territorial Defence or of the Serb army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And along that route --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The full answer didn't make it, I'm told. The question was: Who were those Serbs who were accompanying you? And I understand his answer was, "They were local Serbs from the village of Kljevci," I think or something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is that what you -- thank you for your observation, Mr. Ackerman. Sir, is that what you answered to the question that Madam Fauveau put to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't quite hear what was said, what Mr. Ackerman said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You were asked: "And who were those Serbs who were accompanying you?" What was your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Serbs. Local Serbs from the village of Kljevci.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That clarifies it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: On the journey to Kenjari, you had no problems, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that one day the Serb army came to Kenjari to look for weapons; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the people who came to Kenjari on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You recognised Zeljko Karanovic and Nikola Balac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: I didn't know them in person, but these others said who was who. I mean, my relatives and friends who lived in that village, they knew them all because they had grown up together there.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And these persons, Zeljko Karanovic and Nikola Balac, were also inhabitants of a village in the area of Hrustovo, Kenjari, Kljevci?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And those persons were also members of the Serb Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you stopped at the house of Marko Juric.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: But if you look at the statement that you gave to the Bosnian authorities, on page 2 you said that you were ordered to go to the house of Marko Blazevic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: That must be a mistake, because I didn't know the surname of that man. But it later emerged that his name was Juric and not Blazevic, and Blazevic lives further up.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do they also come from your area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mico Djukic and Milovan Djukic, do they also come from your area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: I think we are mixing up the names. One was called Mico. His legal name was Milutin. And his brother's name was Rade, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And this Mico and Rade Djukic, were they from your region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And they also belonged to the Serb defence -- Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: I am going to say the Serbian army. Now, whether they were in the Territorial Defence or not, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: But that is really because you make no distinction between the Territorial Defence, paramilitaries, and the Serb army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: I'm unable to judge who is what.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you were in the house of Dujo Banovic, you heard somebody cry out, "A bomb."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And then you heard the explosion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: But you personally didn't see the person who threw the bomb.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that when you jumped out of the window that you were able to hear what was going on in the house but that you were not able to see what was happening; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And at a certain point in time you heard shots.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Later when they forced them out of the house they executed them.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: At that point were you able to see the Muslims outside the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And were you able to see the Serbs outside the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So really you didn't see the people firing the shots.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that when you were in the Krings camp, during the first two weeks you were guarded by military reservists. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: They were not military policemen. They were ordinary reservists.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that those reservists didn't beat you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And while those reservists were guarding you, you received food from members of your family; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And the members of your family, were they able to come and see you and visit you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And in fact during those two weeks in Krings when the reservists -- army reservists were there, you were not mistreated; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that on the day you were released, a guard brought a document and that you were released on the basis of that document. Did you receive a document when you were released?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what was written on that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT16
utterances.text: It was a discharge paper. I don't know exactly what it said. It said that I was being released from Krings, my name and surname, and the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Is there re-examination? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sir, there being no further questions, that brings your testimony here to an end. I wish to thank you on behalf of the Tribunal for having come over here to give evidence in this trial. You will now be escorted out of the courtroom by the court usher and returned to your country. If you need any assistance, please let us know. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Anything else before we close?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anything else before we close? Okay. I thank you all for your cooperation. We will be sitting again on Monday in the afternoon, and we'll take it up from there. The next witness is 7.62; correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Have a nice weekend.
